source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:22 ('הקל defective — when the voice of Jacob is lean in the synagogues and study-houses, the hands of Esau rule'; Bereshit Rabbah 65 via the Yefeh Toar; the Jerusalem-aggadah cited)
claim_en: THE LEAN VOICE OF JACOB: הקל קול יעקב ('THE VOICE is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are Esau's hands') — the sentence's first voice-word written DEFECTIVE, and it is UNIQUE in the whole Torah (one token of the lean the-voice), while its own echo in the same breath (קול) runs full: the midrash rides exactly this — when Jacob's voice goes lean, Esau's hands prevail. Letter and derash in one clause.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:3 ('צידה written, ציד read — the extra heh written and not read; the Ramah: the Torah's ONE extra-heh after dalet'; the Masorah's disputed pair-list named); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 27:3 (the five laws of slaughter in the extra heh)
claim_en: THE HUNT'S EXTRA LETTER: צודה לי צידה ('hunt me GAME') — WRITTEN with a closing heh, READ without it (SNAPSHOT carries both tokens side by side, the written and the read): the Ramah rules it the Torah's one extra-heh of its kind, and the Kitzur reads the surplus letter as the FIVE laws of ritual slaughter Isaac taught with the hunt — the heh (five) hanging unread on the game-word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:29 (the Ramah's Masorah: 'first lean — written one vav, read doubled; second plene two vavs; every such form in the Torah likewise save two lean')
claim_en: THE BOW-VERBS, ONE LEAN ONE FULL: וישתחו לך לאמים ('peoples shall BOW to you') — the blessing's first bow-verb WRITTEN with one closing vav and READ doubled (ktiv-qere pair on SNAPSHOT), while the second in the same verse (וישתחוו 'and nations bow') is written with BOTH vavs — exactly the Ramah's filing: the lean future-bow and the full one side by side in Jacob's blessing (the Kitzur counts the lean vav toward the six generations Edom served, David to Yoram).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:29 ('ארריך ומברכיך plene yod; the Ramah: THREE in the language, all plene — those who bless you of Lech Lecha, of here, of Balak')
claim_en: THE BLESS-CAREER'S MIDDLE STATION: ומברכיך ('and THOSE WHO BLESS YOU — blessed') — plene with the yod, completing the Ramah's three-token list letter-exact on SNAPSHOT: bare מברכיך at Abraham's call (12:3) and Balaam's mouth (Num 24:9), prefixed ומברכיך here — the whole career plene (run 4's vocalization-law crown gains its middle link).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:29 (the bare pair)
claim_en: ...the bare pair censused: מברכיך twice — the call and Balaam.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:19 ('the accent CUTS: I am — who I am; but Esau is your firstborn'; the Zohar page and Bereshit Rabbah 65:16, R. Levi's Ten-Commandments reading, named)
claim_en: THE PAUSE THAT SAVES THE SENTENCE: אנכי עשו בכרך ('I am... Esau your firstborn') — the tradition reads Jacob's words as two clauses cut at אנכי ('I am [who I am]; Esau is your firstborn'), and SNAPSHOT's own accent carries the cut: אנכי stands under pashta (the postpositive disjunctive) — the pause the Zohar and R. Levi ride is in the letter's music.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:19 ('מצידי plene yod in all our books and the Ramah, against the old tikkun's lean note')
claim_en: מצידי ('eat OF MY GAME') — plene with the yod as the Ramah rules explicitly, the old correction-book's lean variant declined. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:19 + 27:31 ('תברכני — the nun DAGESHED'; the Chizkuni and the Michlol Yofi concur)
claim_en: תברכני ('that your soul may BLESS ME') — the nun dageshed as ruled, and the SAME pressed nun returns in Esau's mouth at 27:31 (builder-asserted): the two sons' bless-me requests carry one irregular dot — Jacob's disguised and Esau's desperate, pointed identically.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:27 ('ויברכהו — the resh with sheva ALONE per our custom'; likewise ברכו there, ברכני at 27:34, ברכו at 27:41)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY, STATIONS FIVE THROUGH EIGHT: the blessing chapter's four ruled bless-tokens — ויברכהו and ברכו (27:27), ברכני (27:34), ברכו (27:41) — all wanted with the resh in plain sheva 'per our custom'; SNAPSHOT points HATAF PATACH at every one (builder-asserted across the four): the sheva-vs-hataf codex split now counts EIGHT stations, all on resh (with gen_45's boundary result standing: the ayin stays bare). Watchlist.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:1 ('מראת — lean in the Hilleli and all the books, the Masorah: unique-lean; the Ramah concurs'); Kitzur on 27:1 (the bribery and idol-smoke readings)
claim_en: מראת ('his eyes dimmed FROM SEEING') — UNIQUE in the Torah and written lean as all the books rule; the Kitzur's readings ride the dimming (the bribe of Esau's game; the smoke of the wives' idols — the gematria named, unclaimed).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:12 ('כמתעתע — the Masorah: unique; the first tav RAFEH; so the precise manuscripts')
claim_en: כמתעתע ('I shall seem to him AS A MOCKER') — UNIQUE in the Torah, the first tav soft as ruled: Jacob's feared word appears once in the letter, at his own hesitation.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:11 ('שער lean — the printed yod an error against the Masorah'; the four-list dispute with Minchat Kohen's retraction: 'only the two found lean'); on 27:23 (the hands' שערת)
claim_en: THE HAIRY BROTHER'S LEAN LETTERS: איש שער ('Esau my brother is a HAIRY man,' 27:11) — written without the yod (the printer's yod called an error), and the hands' שערת ('hairy,' 27:23) lean likewise: SNAPSHOT sides with Minchat Kohen's retraction — the TWO Esau-tokens lean — while the fuller four-list (which read the Yom Kippur GOATS' identical consonants into the family) stays a named dispute.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:33 ('ואברכהו — the vav in QAMATZ, the past-converting; the Masorah's pair: the future one in patach — I called him AND BLESSED HIM'; Ibn Ezra and the Radak explained); Kitzur (the Abraham-link)
claim_en: ואברכהו ('I ate of all before you came — AND I BLESSED HIM; indeed, blessed he shall be') — the vav in QAMATZ (the past-tense converter, as Ibn Ezra explains the guttural's compensation), against its Masorah-pair in PATACH — 'I called him and I SHALL BLESS him' (Abraham's verse, Isa 51:2; edge): Isaac's blessing sealed in the past vowel, Abraham's promised in the future one — and the Kitzur reads the pair as the blessing of Abraham passing to Jacob.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:33 ('ויאמר מי איפוא — the initials: HIS MOTHER — who was the broker in the matter? Rebecca')
claim_en: HIS MOTHER IN THE INITIALS: ויאמר מי אפוא ('and he said: WHO THEN...?' — Isaac's great trembling) — the three words open ו-מ-א, the letters of אמו ('his mother'): the Kitzur answers Isaac's who-question from the verse's own initials — the broker was Rebecca.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:34 (the Masorah's mirror-set: 'Esau CRIED a cry — Mordechai CRIED a cry; the Torah: their cry I have heard — Ezra: their cry You heard at the Sea'; with its laugh-mnemonic)
claim_en: THE CRY THAT RETURNS: ויצעק צעקה ('and Esau CRIED an exceedingly great and bitter CRY') — the doubled cry-figure stands ONCE in the Torah (adjacency-verified), and the Masorah's mirror is Mordechai's ('he CRIED a great and bitter cry,' Esth 4:1; edge): the tradition's measure-for-measure — Esau's extorted cry repaid on Haman's decree-day, the two bitter cries filed as one pair.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:35 ('במרמה — two in the Masorah: he came WITH DECEIT; the sons of Jacob answered WITH DECEIT — because he deceived his father, his sons came with deceit')
claim_en: THE DECEIT REPAID IN KIND: במרמה ('your brother came WITH DECEIT and took your blessing') — exactly TWICE in the Torah: Jacob's deceit here and his own sons' answer at Shechem ('the sons of Jacob answered... WITH DECEIT,' 34:13) — the word returns on the deceiver's house, the Kitzur's measure-for-measure in a two-token lock.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:36 ('ברכתי — three in the Masorah: he TOOK my blessing; TAKE, please, my blessing; I will COMMAND my blessing')
claim_en: THE BLESSING'S LADDER: ברכתי ('my blessing') — FOUR consonantal tokens in the Torah, and they preach in sequence: Esau's 'he took MY BLESSING' (27:36), Jacob's restitution 'take, please, MY BLESSING' to Esau's own face (33:11), and God's 'I will command MY BLESSING' (Lev 25:21) — the Kitzur's three noun-stations: taken, returned, commanded; the fourth token is the verb at Ishmael's promise ('I have BLESSED him,' 17:20) — the homograph split named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:40 ('ואת אחיך תעבד — defective, and every serve-token in the Torah likewise'; Bereshit Rabbah 67: 'if worthy — he shall be served; if not — he shall serve')
claim_en: THE TWO-WAY SERVE-VERB AGAIN: ואת אחיך תעבד ('and your brother you shall SERVE' — Esau's sentence) — defective, and the whole family lean: תעבד stands TWELVE times in the Torah with NO plene token (builder-asserted), from Cain's soil (4:12) through the labor-commandment (Exod 20:9) to this verse; Bereshit Rabbah 67 reads the oracle's reversal in the missing vav exactly as at the twins' birth (frozen G43-03): the brothers' service stays two-way in the letter.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:28 ('ויתן לך — TEN words in the verse, against the Ten Utterances his twelve sons would receive')
claim_en: THE TEN-WORD DEW-BLESSING: ויתן לך ('may God give you of the dew of heaven...') — the verse counts exactly TEN words, the Kitzur's count against the Ten Utterances; machine-checked by the verse-length instrument.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:29 ('this blessing holds TWENTY-SIX words — he blessed him with the honored Name, whose count is twenty-six')
claim_en: ...and the WHOLE blessing (27:28-29) counts TWENTY-SIX read words — ten in the dew-verse, sixteen in the peoples-verse (the SNAPSHOT token-count of seventeen includes the written/read bow-verb pair counted once in the reading, builder-asserted): the blessing carries the four-letter Name's own number, exactly the Kitzur's arithmetic.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 27:29 ('הוה — two in the Masorah: BE lord to your brothers; for to the snow He says: FALL to earth — by Jacob's merit the rain and snow descend')
claim_en: הוה ('BE lord to your brothers') — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair-leg is the snow-command ('for to the snow He says: BE upon the earth,' Job 37:6; edge): the Kitzur hangs the rains on Jacob's lordship-word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:37 ('ולכה — this alone written with the closing heh in the Torah'; Rabbenu Bachya cited)
claim_en: ולכה אפוא מה אעשה בני ('and FOR YOU then, what shall I do, my son?') — the for-you word written with the extra closing heh, the Torah's only such dative (the two consonantal look-alikes are Balaam's go-imperatives, Num 22:17 and 23:7 — a different word): Isaac's emptied-hands question carries one letter more than it needs, as Bachya reads it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:40 ('ועל חרבך תחיה — HALF THE BOOK in verses')
claim_en: THE SWORD AT THE BOOK'S MIDDLE: ועל חרבך תחיה ('by your sword you shall live') — the Masorah marks this verse HALF OF GENESIS by verse-count (its total: 1,534). SNAPSHOT's versification counts 1,533 verses with 27:40 standing 768th — one seam off the arithmetic middle: the verse-count split between the Masorah's total and the codex line's is itself the finding (variance, named; builder-computed ordinals).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:18; Onkelos Genesis 27:19
claim_en: WHETHER THE SENTENCE LIES IS DISPUTED ACROSS THE DECLARED SHELF. R. Levi acquits it by re-punctuation: 'I am' - destined to receive the commandments - 'Esau is your firstborn', two statements rather than one lie. Onkelos declines the defence and renders the line straight, at both 27:19 and 27:24. One member mounts an equivocation defence; the other refuses it and lets the sentence stand as it reads.

check.note: An equivocation defence mounted by one member of the shelf and declined by the other at the same verse.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:20; Bereshit Rabbah 65:21
claim_en: THE VOICE AND THE HANDS ARE READ AS A STANDING MECHANISM WITH A TOGGLE. Jacob rules only by his voice and Esau only by his hands, and R. Berekhya supplies the switch: when the voice MURMURS in complaint the hands dominate - the people complained, and Amalek came - and when it cries aloud they fail. The weaver's test follows from it: circulate their synagogues, and if children's voices are heard you cannot touch them. The claim is then extended to the liturgy - when Israel recites the Shema the angels fall silent - with R. Yehuda bar Ilai's dark counter-reading recorded, in which the voice is screaming at what the hands have done.

check.note: A dominance mechanism with an explicit toggle condition, extended to liturgy, with the tragic reading preserved.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 66:3
claim_en: THE CHAIN MAPS ITS OWN FOUR-PART CANON ONTO THIS BLESSING. The blessing's items are typologized several ways, and the summit reading assigns them to the divisions of the tradition itself: the dew of the heavens is SCRIPTURE, the fat of the land is MISHNAH, the grain is TALMUD, the wine is the narrative lore. The two-shelves architecture this project reconstructs is here drawn by the tradition in its own words, on a narrative verse. The extra letter opening the blessing is separately read as give AND GIVE AGAIN, divine giving as a repeatable operation.

check.note: The tradition mapping its own canonical divisions onto a narrative blessing's terms.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 66:5
claim_en: THE LAW CORPUS'S OWN HOMICIDE VERB IS READ BACK INTO THIS NARRATIVE. 'From his hunt' at 27:30 is glossed as armed to hunt his life, and the gloss is carried by the non-intent clause of the manslaughter statute at Exodus 21:13, which uses the same verb. The chapter this project has read most deeply is thereby wired into a narrative scene by a shared root, and the door geometry of the verse - the hinged leaf, the doubled going-out - is read alongside it.

check.note: A narrative verb glossed by the identical verb in the homicide statute, wiring the law corpus into the story.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 66:6
claim_en: A LIVE LITURGICAL RULE IS SEATED ON THE CURSE-AND-BLESS CLAUSE. The taught rule is quoted: an idolater who blesses the Name - answer amen after him; one who blesses BY the Name - do not. R. Yishmael's double answer is recorded with it, given to the gentile who blessed him and the one who cursed him alike: your response is already stated - our verse both times. A standing practice ruling anchored to a line of narrative blessing.

check.note: A practice ruling about responding amen, anchored to this verse and applied in both directions.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 67:2; Bereshit Rabbah 67:12
claim_en: A DEED-LAW MAXIM IS APPLIED TO THE BLESSING, TWICE. R. Elazar's rule is that RATIFICATION OF A DOCUMENT IS ONLY BY ITS SIGNATORIES, and it is deployed to answer the objection that the blessings stood only by deceit: the verse's own 'indeed he shall be blessed' is the signatory's ratification. The maxim is stated at 27:33 and again at its home seat in gen_47's 28:1, where the blessings are called uncertain in his hand until he summoned and blessed knowingly. An instrument-law rule governing the validity of a spoken blessing.

check.note: A document-ratification maxim used to validate a spoken blessing obtained by deception.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 67:5
claim_en: AN ACQUISITION MAXIM FROM THE CASE SHELF IS USED TO VOID THE ELDER'S CLAIM. Asked why the lordship blessing is answered first, the chain replies: I made him KING over you - and your blessings are his, because WHATEVER A SLAVE OWNS BELONGS TO HIS MASTER. The property rule of the servitude corpus is deployed as narrative logic to extinguish a claim, exactly the move the machine records at gen_42's tribunal with the gift-and-severance clause.

check.note: A slave-property acquisition maxim used to extinguish a narrative claim.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 67:4
claim_en: A CRY IS BOOKED AGAINST A CRY ACROSS THE CANON, AT THE EXACT PHRASE. The chain holds that God is not lax but patient and collecting, and the ledger entry is precise: the one great and bitter cry at 27:34 is repaid in Mordechai's great and bitter cry. The repayment is carried by the shared phrase rather than by theme - measure for measure tracked at the level of words.

check.note: A measure-for-measure repayment tracked by an exact repeated phrase across books.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 67:4; Onkelos Genesis 27:35
claim_en: THE WORD FOR THE DECEPTION IS RE-GRADED BY BOTH MEMBERS ALIKE. R. Yochanan re-reads 'with cunning' as WITH THE WISDOM OF HIS TORAH; Onkelos renders the same word WITH WISDOM, and turns 'took your blessing' into RECEIVED your blessing, legalizing the taking into a receipt. Two members of the declared reading softening one accusation in the same direction, and the translation going further by converting the verb of taking into a verb of conveyance.

check.note: An accusatory term re-graded identically by both members, with the translation additionally legalizing the transfer verb.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 67:7; Onkelos Genesis 27:40
claim_en: A CONDITION FOR THE END OF SUBJECTION IS WRITTEN INTO THE VERSE BY THE TRANSLATION. R. Yosei bar Chalafta reads the closing clause as a yoke-removal condition: when you see your brother throw off the yoke of the Torah, you will dominate. Onkelos does not gloss this - it renders it as the plain sense: WHEN HIS SONS TRANSGRESS THE WORDS OF THE TORAH, you will remove his yoke from your neck. A historical-conditional supplied as translation, and the largest convergence in this sweep; the same verse also carries the reading that the sword be SHEATHED and the double-read of serve-or-eradicate.

check.note: A conditional historical rule stated by the midrash and rendered as the verse's plain sense by the translation.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 91:11
claim_en: THE PARTICLE OF THE TREMBLING IS REPAID AT THE SAME PARTICLE. Isaac's 'who THEN' at 27:33 is read against Jacob's own 'if so THEN' much later, with the question put in Jacob's mouth: can the trembling I caused my father be shaking me here? Machine-checked in our corpus: the particle stands exactly four times in the Torah - twice in this scene, at 27:33 and 27:37, once at 43:11 where the repayment is booked, and once in Exodus. A measure-for-measure wire carried by a rare word, and every occurrence accounted for.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 43:8
claim_en: THIS VERSE CARRIES THE MIDDLE LEG OF A THREE-WORD BLESSING CENSUS. The chain counts three patriarchal blessing-words - with everything, FROM everything, everything - and the middle leg is 'I ate FROM ALL' at 27:33. Machine-checked: the three words stand at 24:1, at this verse, and at 33:11, exactly where the census places them, one to each patriarch.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:12
claim_en: A DEATH-ANXIETY RULE IS SEATED ON THE VERSE THAT STATES THE ANXIETY. R. Yehoshua ben Korcha holds that on reaching within five years of a parent's age one begins to fear death, and the arithmetic is supplied for Isaac at 123 against Sarah's 127. The verse's own 'I know not the day of my death' is the anchor, and the chain hangs a seven-item census of hidden things on it - the day of death, the day of consolation, the depth of judgment, the source of profit, another's heart, the fetus, and the fall of the empire.

check.note: A psychological rule with an arithmetic trigger, anchored to a verse that states the fear.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:14
claim_en: THE TAKING OF THE KIDS IS LICENSED BY A MARRIAGE CONTRACT AND TYPOLOGIZED TO THE ATONEMENT RITE. The two kids are read as hers by right - Isaac wrote her a food clause of two kids each day - so the mother's instruction is covered by the marriage document, not a theft. And the doubled 'good' is read twice over: good for you, since the blessings ride on them, and good for your sons, since through them atonement comes on the Day of Atonement - the two goats of the rite typologized from these two kids.

check.note: A narrative taking licensed by a marriage contract's terms and simultaneously read as a cult typology.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 76:6
claim_en: A CHARACTER ARGUES HIS CASE OUT OF THE LAW CORPUS. Jacob's later fear - lest he smite me, mother with children - is held by the chain against the Torah's own mercy statutes: the prohibition on taking the mother with the offspring, and the rule against slaughtering an animal and its young on one day. The threat is measured against the standing law, which makes a narrative prayer into a legal argument.

check.note: A character's prayer read as an argument from two specific mercy statutes.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 75:8
claim_en: THE BLESSING IS RATIFIED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE FROM ABOVE. Every clause Isaac blessed below is matched by a corresponding blessing from above with its own proof verse - the dew to the dew verse, the fat to the rain verse, the peoples-serve clause to the kings-as-caregivers verse, the lordship clause to the uppermost-over-nations verse. The blessing is thereby a two-signature instrument, the same document-thinking the chain applies with its ratification maxim. The section also answers why he is blessed again at 28:1: he saw the exiles coming and gave him the blessings of exile.

check.note: A blessing matched clause-for-clause with a countersigning verse, making it a two-party instrument.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 99:5
claim_en: THE TREMBLING IS RE-EXPLAINED AS THE MOMENT AN ENDING WAS CONCEALED. Isaac sought to bless the elder and to reveal the End; his sense was stripped from him, he began to tremble, and found nothing to say but 'indeed he shall be blessed'. On this reading the chapter's central emotional event is not fear at the deception but the withdrawal of a revelation, paired with Jacob's own concealment later in the corpus - and it stands beside the other readings of the same trembling rather than replacing them.

check.note: The scene's central emotion re-assigned to a withheld revelation, preserved alongside rival readings.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:9
claim_en: THE THREE-DEMANDS LADDER OPENED IN FULL, AND IT SPLITS THREE WAYS. Bereshit Rabbah 65:9 claims that aging, suffering and illness are each unwritten until a patriarch demanded them - aging at 24:1, suffering at this verse's dimmed eyes, illness at 48:1. All three legs were opened against our corpus under guard 3, and they do not stand together. LEG ONE FAILS: the word for old stands five times before 24:1, at 18:11, 18:12, 18:13, 19:4 and 19:31, with 18:11 carrying the identical phrase - recorded at gen_40 and not applied. LEG TWO CANNOT BE A WORD-CENSUS AT ALL: the root for chastisement does not occur anywhere in Genesis, its first Torah appearance being Leviticus 26:18, and it does not occur in this verse either - so the suffering leg is a claim about the first recorded affliction, not about ink, and is carried as interpretive. LEG THREE HOLDS EXACTLY: the word for illness stands ONCE in Genesis and it is at 48:1, precisely where the chain says illness was granted - three tokens in the whole Torah, the other two in Exodus and Deuteronomy. Machine-checked. A three-part structure of which one part is exact, one is false, and one is not the kind of claim that can be checked this way.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:5; Bereshit Rabbah 65:8; Bereshit Rabbah 65:10
claim_en: WHY HIS EYES DIMMED IS A RECORDED FOUR-WAY DISPUTE, NOT A DETAIL. Because he exonerated a wicked man for a bribe, the bribe being the game in his mouth; because the ministering angels wept at the binding and THEIR TEARS FELL INTO HIS EYES, which wires the altar of gen_38 into this verse; because he gazed at the Presence on that altar, the decree deferred to old age; or, flatly, SO THAT JACOB COULD COME AND TAKE THE BLESSINGS - the dimming as arranged mechanism. The narrative's enabling condition is given four incompatible causes and none is dropped.

check.note: The enabling condition of a whole chapter given four incompatible causes, all preserved.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:6; Onkelos Genesis 27:13
claim_en: THE DECEPTION IS GIVEN BOTH A MOTIVE AND A LICENCE, ONE FROM EACH MEMBER. The chain rules the mother's motive: not that she loved one son more, but that the other should not enter and MISLEAD THAT ELDER into a false verdict - the act re-graded as preventing a miscarriage of judgment. And Onkelos supplies the licence, replacing her self-curse with IT WAS SAID TO ME IN PROPHECY THAT THE CURSES WILL NOT COME UPON YOU - writing the matriarch-prophecy doctrine, which gen_47 states outright, into this verse as its plain sense. The unit's demandee-mismatch machine thereby receives its motive from one member of the declared reading and its authorization from the other.

check.note: A single act supplied with its motive by the midrash and its authorization by the translation, independently.
